draft.briefing: Hey, you're at Cherai Beach! It's one of the most visited beaches in Kerala, up on the northern side of Vypin Island, about 25 km from downtown Kochi.
draft.hungryLine: This is seafood country, so look for prawns, squid, fish molly and Kochi's famous Meen Molagitta Curry.

moodReplies.show-me-around: The beach is a 3 min walk. Up the road at Munambam you'll find a big fishing harbour and lots of boat-making yards.
moodReplies.somewhere-to-chill: Grab a spot on the sand and watch the locals play beach volleyball. Cherai is famous for it.
moodReplies.surprise-me: From Munambam Muziris beach, just north of here, you can see the mouth of the Periyar, the district's major river.

spots.name: Cherai Beach
spots.detail: 3 min walk · One of Kerala's most visited beaches

spots.name: Munambam
spots.detail: All around you · Fishing harbour and boat-making yards

tips.title: Come for Onam.
tips.body: Kerala's ten-day state festival runs somewhere between mid-August and mid-September.

tips.title: Join a volleyball game.
tips.body: Cherai is a favourite with locals for beach volleyball, and beach football is popular too.

story.title: A meeting place
story.body: Arabs, Chinese, Portuguese, Dutch, English and more have all come through Kochi. You can taste the mix in the food today.

story.title: Carnival begins
story.body: The Cochin Carnival started as part of Portuguese New Year celebrations. It still runs from December 20 to January 2.

story.title: Fishing families
story.body: Munambam, at the north end of Vypin Island, lives mostly by fishing. It has a major government fishing harbour and many boat-making yards.

story.title: Kochi's beach
story.body: Cherai is one of the most visited beaches in the state, about 20 km from Cochin International Airport.
